metadata.title: Why Microsoft is not this portfolio manager's stock pick

content.text:
Niles Investment Management founder and portfolio manager Dan Niles shares his perspective on Microsoft (MSFT) in the AI landscape.
one more name I would love to get your take on is Microsoft. Um, only because I was just listening to Brian Belsky. He was on Josh Brown's podcast and you know, Belsky's been doing this a long time, smart guy and then they were just kind of talking about names and Belsky mentioned he likes Microsoft here.
And he was saying, listen, strong consistent earnings growth and I I think he mentioned uh, you know, 78 billion in total cash, right? Uh, what's not to like? I'm just curious to get your thoughts, Dan. Do you agree? Is Microsoft a compelling investment here?
Well, that's what makes markets, people can have different opinions, right? No, I don't think Microsoft's a compelling investment for one reason. Do they themselves have a leading large language model?
No, they don't.
They get access to that through chat GPT and open AI.
And so that's to me is a huge issue when it comes to Microsoft. The second thing is, if you're in a world where you're talking about AI disintermediating products from companies and you saw that this morning, which is potentially why Microsoft's down. You saw Starbucks, something came out that said, hey, they're spending 400 million bucks a year on software and they're using um AI models to try to get out of that spend.
Some of which is with Microsoft and some of which is with IBM, which was also down earlier today.
So, that's why for me, I go, yeah, I I don't like Microsoft because you have that risk and I fundamentally believe given their 27% ownership in Open AI, I I think Open AI has an issue because they're caught between Anthropic, which is from the beginning focused on corporate, where corporations are willing to pay. Only 5% of Anthropic's consumers are willing to pay, right? Because Google's trained you, if you're a consumer, you got everything for free.
And then on the other side of it, you have Google on the consumer side, which people are very used to entering queries into Google, they're dominant on the consumer side.
So I think between Google on the consumer side and Thropic on the corporate side, and Microsoft not having their own model and granted they're entitled to some of the IP from Open AI and you know, it's unclear to me how all of that's necessarily going to work.
But I have other names that I obviously can like better. Meta owns their own large language model and it trades much cheaper than Microsoft as an example of that.
